title: Applicability, scope & role determination
desc: Determine whether and where GDPR applies to you (EU establishment, or offering goods/services to or monitoring people in the EU/UK) and, for each processing activity, whether you act as controller, joint controller or processor.

title: Principles of processing
desc: Process personal data lawfully, fairly and transparently; for specified purposes (purpose limitation); minimised; accurate; kept no longer than necessary (storage limitation); and securely (integrity & confidentiality). The controller must be able to demonstrate compliance (accountability).

title: Lawful basis for processing
desc: Every processing activity must rely on at least one Article 6 lawful basis: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests.

title: Conditions for consent
desc: Where consent is relied upon, be able to demonstrate it was freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous; make it as easy to withdraw as to give.

title: Child's consent (information society services)
desc: For online services offered directly to children, consent is valid only where the child is at least 16 (Member States may lower to not below 13); otherwise obtain/verify parental authorisation.

title: Special categories of data
desc: Processing of special-category data (health, biometrics, race, politics, religion, sex life, etc.) is prohibited unless an Article 9(2) condition applies (e.g. explicit consent, employment law, substantial public interest).

title: Criminal convictions data
desc: Processing of personal data on criminal convictions and offences is allowed only under official authority control or where authorised by Union/Member State law with appropriate safeguards.

title: Processing not requiring identification
desc: You need not maintain, acquire or process extra data solely to identify a data subject for compliance; if you cannot identify them, inform them where possible (rights in Art. 15-20 may then not apply).

title: Transparent information & modalities
desc: Provide information and handle rights requests in a concise, transparent, intelligible form; respond without undue delay and within one month (extendable by two months); generally free of charge.

title: Information where data collected from the person
desc: At collection, inform the data subject of controller identity, purposes, legal basis, recipients, transfers, retention, their rights and (where relevant) automated decision-making.

title: Information where data not obtained from the person
desc: Where data is obtained indirectly, provide equivalent information within a reasonable period (at latest one month), including the categories of data and their source.

title: Right of access
desc: On request, confirm whether you process the person's data, provide access and the prescribed information, and a copy of the data.

title: Right to rectification
desc: Rectify inaccurate personal data without undue delay and complete incomplete data.

title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
desc: Erase personal data without undue delay where a ground applies (no longer necessary, consent withdrawn, unlawful processing, etc.), subject to exemptions.

title: Right to restriction of processing
desc: Restrict processing in the defined cases (accuracy contested, unlawful processing, etc.).

title: Notification to recipients
desc: Communicate any rectification, erasure or restriction to each recipient of the data unless impossible/disproportionate; inform the data subject of recipients if requested.

title: Right to data portability
desc: Where processing is by consent or contract and automated, provide the person's data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and transmit it to another controller where feasible.

title: Right to object
desc: Allow objection to processing based on public task/legitimate interests (and always for direct marketing, which must then stop).

title: Automated decision-making & profiling
desc: Individuals have the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions with legal/similarly significant effect, except in defined cases with safeguards (human intervention, contest).

title: Restrictions & exemptions to rights
desc: Where Union or Member State law (in the UK, DPA 2018 Schedules 2-4) restricts a right - e.g. crime prevention, legal privilege, third-party data - apply the exemption case by case and record the justification.

title: Responsibility of the controller
desc: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and demonstrate compliance, reviewed and updated as needed; include data-protection policies where proportionate.

title: Data protection by design & by default
desc: Embed data-protection principles (e.g. minimisation, pseudonymisation) into processing design, and by default process only the data necessary for each purpose.

title: Joint controllers
desc: Where you jointly determine purposes/means with another controller, agree and make transparent your respective responsibilities.

title: Representative of non-EU controllers/processors
desc: Controllers/processors not established in the EU but in scope of Art. 3(2) must designate an EU representative (with limited exceptions).

title: Processor contracts
desc: Use only processors providing sufficient guarantees, bound by a written Article 28 contract with the mandated terms (documented instructions, confidentiality, security, sub-processors, deletion/return, audits).

title: Processing under authority
desc: Ensure anyone acting under your authority processes personal data only on your instructions.

title: Records of Processing Activities (ROPA)
desc: Maintain records of processing activities as controller/processor (purposes, categories, recipients, transfers, retention, security measures). Exemption for organisations <250 employees unless risky/non-occasional/special-category.

title: Cooperation with the supervisory authority
desc: Cooperate, on request, with the supervisory authority in the performance of its tasks.

title: Security of processing
desc: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for a level of security appropriate to the risk - e.g. pseudonymisation/encryption, confidentiality/integrity/availability/resilience, restore ability, and regular testing.

title: Breach notification to the supervisory authority
desc: Notify the supervisory authority of a personal-data breach without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours, unless unlikely to risk individuals' rights; document all breaches.

title: Breach communication to data subjects
desc: Where a breach is likely to result in high risk to individuals, communicate it to them without undue delay (with exceptions, e.g. data was encrypted).

title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
desc: Carry out a DPIA before processing likely to result in high risk (e.g. large-scale special-category, systematic monitoring, automated decisions).

title: Prior consultation
desc: Consult the supervisory authority before processing where a DPIA indicates high residual risk you cannot mitigate.

title: Designation of a DPO
desc: Designate a Data Protection Officer where required (public authority; core activities involve large-scale regular monitoring or large-scale special-category data).

title: Position of the DPO
desc: Involve the DPO in all data-protection matters, provide resources and independence, and no dismissal for performing the role.

title: Tasks of the DPO
desc: The DPO informs/advises, monitors compliance, advises on DPIAs, and is the contact point for the supervisory authority and data subjects.

title: Codes of conduct & certification (optional)
desc: Adherence to an approved code of conduct (Art. 40-41) or certification mechanism (Art. 42-43) may be used to demonstrate compliance. Optional, not mandatory.

title: General principle for transfers
desc: Transfers of personal data outside the EEA are permitted only under the conditions of Chapter V, ensuring the level of protection is not undermined (including onward transfers).

title: Transfers on an adequacy decision
desc: Transfers may occur to a country/sector/organisation the Commission has decided ensures an adequate level of protection, without further authorisation.

title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
desc: Absent adequacy, transfer only with appropriate safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses, binding corporate rules, approved codes/certifications) with enforceable rights and remedies.

title: Binding corporate rules
desc: Intra-group transfers may rely on binding corporate rules approved by the competent supervisory authority meeting the Art. 47 content requirements.

title: Transfers not authorised by Union law
desc: Third-country court/authority orders to transfer data are recognised only if based on an international agreement (e.g. MLAT).

title: Derogations for specific situations
desc: In the absence of adequacy/safeguards, transfer only under a specific derogation (explicit consent, contract necessity, important public interest, legal claims, vital interests, etc.).

title: Lead supervisory authority & main establishment
desc: If you process across borders within the EU, identify your main establishment and therefore your lead supervisory authority (one-stop-shop); know which authority you notify breaches to and deal with.

title: Complaints & remedies readiness
desc: Individuals may complain to a supervisory authority, seek judicial remedies and be represented by a not-for-profit body. Tell them so in privacy notices and request responses, and be able to handle complaints and regulator enquiries.

title: Right to compensation & liability
desc: Any person suffering material or non-material damage from an infringement has the right to compensation from the controller/processor.

title: Administrative fines
desc: Infringements are subject to administrative fines up to ?10M or 2% of global annual turnover (lower tier) or ?20M or 4% (higher tier, e.g. breach of principles or data-subject rights), whichever is higher.

title: Penalties (Member State)
desc: Member States lay down additional penalties for infringements not covered by Art. 83; they must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

title: Journalism, academic & artistic expression (where applicable)
desc: If you process personal data for journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purposes, apply the national exemptions that balance data protection with freedom of expression, and document reliance on them.

title: National identification numbers
desc: Use national ID numbers (e.g. social security, national insurance, CNIC) only under the conditions national law sets, with appropriate safeguards and minimal exposure.

title: Employee data
desc: Process employee and candidate data in line with national employment-context rules: transparency, proportionate monitoring, and safeguards for dignity and legitimate interests.

title: Research, statistics & archiving safeguards
desc: Where you process for scientific/historical research, statistics or archiving in the public interest, apply safeguards such as minimisation and pseudonymisation, and rely on any national derogations only as permitted.

title: Professional secrecy obligations
desc: If you are subject to professional secrecy (e.g. legal, medical, financial), reconcile it with data-protection duties and supervisory-authority access as national law provides.

title: Cookies & electronic marketing (ePrivacy / PECR)
desc: Obtain valid consent for non-essential cookies and similar tracking and for electronic direct marketing, per the ePrivacy Directive's national laws (in the UK, PECR). Honour opt-outs, and identify yourself in every marketing message.

title: ICO registration & data protection fee
desc: UK controllers must pay the annual data protection fee to the ICO unless exempt (Data Protection (Charges and Information) Regulations 2018), and keep the registration details current.

title: UK representative
desc: Controllers or processors with no UK establishment that offer goods/services to, or monitor, people in the UK must appoint a UK representative (UK GDPR Art. 27), unless an exception applies.

title: UK international transfers
desc: Restricted transfers out of the UK need UK adequacy regulations, or the ICO's International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA) or UK Addendum to the EU SCCs, plus a documented assessment that the destination's protection is not materially lower (the DUAA 'data protection test').

title: Special category data: DPA 2018 Schedule 1 & appropriate policy document
desc: Where special category or criminal offence data relies on a DPA 2018 Schedule 1 condition, record the condition and, where required, maintain an Appropriate Policy Document explaining compliance and retention.

title: Recognised legitimate interests
desc: Where you rely on a DUAA 'recognised legitimate interest' (e.g. crime prevention, safeguarding, emergencies, national security), record which one applies. No balancing test is needed, but it cannot be used for significant automated decisions.

title: Automated decision-making safeguards (Art. 22A-22D)
desc: For significant decisions based solely on automated processing, inform individuals, let them make representations, obtain human intervention and contest the decision. Special category data needs explicit consent or a substantial public interest condition.

title: Data protection complaints procedure
desc: From 19 June 2026, controllers must make it easy to complain to them (e.g. an electronic form), acknowledge complaints within 30 days, investigate without undue delay, and tell the complainant the outcome.

title: Subject access under UK rules
desc: Answer requests within one month (extendable by two for complex or numerous requests). Searches need only be reasonable and proportionate, and the clock may pause while you seek clarification or ID. Apply DPA 2018 Schedule 2 exemptions case by case.
